reason: The text extensively emphasizes hierarchy throughout the narrative. The opening establishes King Ahasuerus's vast dominion and supreme authority. Multiple passages explicitly organize people hierarchically, using the phrase 'from great to small' (מִגָּדוֹל וְעַד־ קָטָן) to describe rankings. The narrative highlights Vashti's removal for refusing to obey the king's command, establishing that violating hierarchical order has serious consequences. Women are expected to give honor to their husbands in a subordinate relationship. The selection of a new queen emphasizes the king's absolute authority in choosing Esther. Haman's elevation involves placing his seat 'above all the princes,' and the requirement that all servants bow to him emphasizes respect for hierarchical position. Mordecai's rise in status is celebrated and described in detail. Throughout, officials, governors (אֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנִים), and subordinates are clearly ordered under the king's authority. The text presents hierarchy as the natural and proper ordering of the Persian empire.
